raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Use the unified PyTorch accelerator APIs for backend-independent operations in `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer`, following #30679 and existing vLLM usage.

## Claims

- Replace availability checks, device selection, synchronization, and current-stream lookups that do not pass streams to CUDA-specific communication APIs.
- Use `torch.Event` for sharded-RDT slot and quantization dependencies.
- Preserve stream-level synchronization boundaries, NCCL stream interfaces, and CUDA IPC behavior.

## Validation

Passed on Windows with PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu:

- `pre-commit run ruff-check --files <six changed files>`
- `pre-commit run ruff-format --files <six changed files>`
- Direct runs of `tools/pre_commit/check_torch_cuda.py`, `check_spdx_header.py`, `check_init_lazy_imports.py`, and `check_forbidden_imports.py` on the changed files.
- Python AST syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

Attempted with `PYTHONUTF8=1`:

```text
uv run --no-sync -- .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_plan.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_trainer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_producer.py -q
```

Pytest fails while loading the repository conftest because `uvloop` is unavailable in this Windows environment; no tests reached execution. Full pre-commit is blocked by cache permissions and a Git Bash `NtCreateDirectoryObject` failure with a fresh writable cache. The mypy hook could not initialize. Commits include DCO sign-off; the broken commit hooks were bypassed after running the available checks separately.

No GPU transfer test or model evaluation was performed on this CPU-only host. Human line-by-line review and hardware validation remain pending, so this PR is a draft. No output-quality, performance, or new-backend support claim is made.

## Details

### Evidence of existing unified API use in vLLM

These links point to upstream commit `7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a`:

| API / pattern | Existing upstream use |
| --- | --- |
| Availability check followed by device synchronization | [WorkerBase.synchronize_device](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py#L129-L133) uses `torch.accelerator.is_available()` and `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`. |
| Current-stream synchronization | [EPLB communicator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py#L227-L232) already uses `torch.accelerator.current_stream().synchronize()`. |
| Device selection in a background thread | [EPLB async worker](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py#L31-L34) uses `torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device_index)`. |
| Device-index context manager | [PyNcclCommunicator initialization](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl.py#L175-L182) uses `torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index)`. |
| Generic events for cross-thread dependencies | [EPLB CpuGpuEvent](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_utils.py#L49-L59) constructs `torch.Event()`. |
| Current stream queried for an explicit tensor device | [Mooncake embedding backend](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/mooncake_store_embedding/backend.py#L209-L214) records a `torch.Event` on `torch.accelerator.current_stream(tensor.device)`. |

Earlier merged migrations include #36085 (synchronization), #36145 (device count/current device/device selection), and #36144 (device contexts). These establish existing API use; runtime validation of this patch remains pending as described above.

### Compatibility and scope

Generic streams do not expose the `.cuda_stream` field consumed by the current NCCL wrappers. Communication stream lookups and stream constructors/contexts are retained, including sharded-RDT contexts that update vLLM's cached current-stream tracking. Device UUID lookup and CUDA IPC collection also remain unchanged.

The earlier global event migration was reverted in #47668 because `torch.Event` ignored the `blocking` parameter ([upstream explanation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47081#issuecomment-4874967250)). This patch only replaces default, nonblocking events.

Duplicate-work checks covered #30679 and its comments, open PRs mentioning it, and `weight_transfer accelerator`. #57374 overlaps the NCCL post-send availability check and changes that stream lookup through vLLM's helper as part of a new transport. This patch additionally covers IPC, packed-buffer stream tracking, sparse NCCL synchronization, and sharded-RDT device/event handling. #57022, #33225, and #37134 address stream/platform or communicator migrations; their interfaces are retained here. This patch does not add a transport or change rendezvous behavior.

AI assistance was used to implement this change and prepare this description.

## H20 correctness verification — `6f0df167` (2× H20e, torch 2.13.0+cu130)

Verified the PR head `6f0df1675fa109e892c33ee72e7b6cc9ca97e656` (branch `codex/weight-transfer-accelerator`, unmodified; change commit `09dce8f7` on top of merged main `7a64fb8fc9`) on the SGP H20 cluster, node `vllm-sgp-h20-04`, 2-GPU jobs (NVIDIA H20-3e 143 GB, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130).

### Environment

- vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev441+g7a64fb8fc` — the per-commit wheel of the **merge base** (`7a64fb8fc9`) from `wheels.vllm.ai`, installed with `uv pip install --no-deps` into a copy of a prepared CUDA venv, plus `ray==2.56.1`, `nixl==1.5.0`, `orjson`.
- The six changed files were then copied over the installed package, and a pristine copy of the same wheel was kept as the baseline, so both trees are identical apart from this patch.

| file | PR md5 | baseline md5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ipc_engine.py` | `36bfff84` | `a3abe286` |
| `nccl_engine.py` | `8978915f` | `a7a67fa5` |
| `packed_tensor.py` | `a2636c6b` | `e6e18f7b` |
| `sharded_rdt_engine.py` | `aead682b` | `80a7ead0` |
| `sharded_rdt_trainer.py` | `1549c6fa` | `2daa5dad` |
| `sparse_nccl_engine.py` | `e7344617` | `2283b787` |

### Test suite: PR and baseline are identical

```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --import-mode=importlib --no-header -rA \
  tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_plan.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_trainer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_producer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer_m2n.py \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer_nccl_uid.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py
```

| tree | result |
| --- | --- |
| PR | 6 failed, 464 passed, 26 skipped (17:07) |
| merge base `7a64fb8fc9` | 6 failed, 464 passed, 26 skipped (17:01) |

The same six tests fail on both trees with the same messages, so none is caused by this change:

- `test_sharded_rdt_plan.py::TestBakeOnARealModel[gqa-dense|moe|mla-moe]` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'orjson'` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py:10`). The wheel was installed with `--no-deps` on this host; after adding `orjson` all three **pass** on both trees.
- `test_weight_transfer_m2n.py::test_m2n_weight_transfer_between_processes[tcp|uid]` → `nccl._extensions.bindings.nccl_m2n.NCCLReshardError: NCCL Reshard error code 5: NCCL operation queryResult failed: invalid usage`. The m2n engine is not touched by this PR and fails identically on the baseline.
- `test_weight_transfer_nccl_uid.py::test_nccl_weight_transfer_between_processes_uid` → failed with `ray.exceptions.GetTimeoutError` inside the full pass on both trees, and **passes** on both in the rerun below, i.e. environment/load sensitivity rather than this change.

Rerun of only those six tests after `orjson` was added: PR **4 passed, 2 failed**; baseline **4 passed, 2 failed**, the two failures being the m2n cases above.

The 26 skips are environmental: 23 × `modelexpress_rl` not installed, 2 × m2n variants that need 3/4 GPUs, 1 × `cupy` missing.

### Runtime API equivalence on H20 (7/7 pass)

`torch.accelerator.current_stream()` returns a generic `torch.Stream` on torch 2.13, so these are behaviour checks of each substituted call against its `torch.cuda.*` counterpart:

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `current_stream()` is the default stream (drains already-enqueued default-stream work) | pass |
| `current_stream(torch.device)` targets that device and does not change the current device | pass |
| `device_index(int)` context manager sets and restores the current device, including tensor placement | pass |
| `set_device_index(int)` inside a worker thread (engine proc/quant-thread pattern) | pass |
| `torch.Event()` `record`/`synchronize`/`wait` on `torch.cuda.Stream`s, with cross-stream ordering | pass |
| `torch.Event()` built on one thread, recorded on the proc stream, waited on the quant stream (engine pattern) | pass |
| `accelerator.synchronize()` drains default-stream work (4.7 ms vs 4.5 ms for `cuda.synchronize()` over the same matmul) | pass |

Compatibility observation that backs the PR's design note: on torch 2.13 the generic wrappers do **not** carry the CUDA-only attributes — `torch.Stream` has no `.cuda_stream` (it has `synchronize`/`query`/`record_event`/`wait_stream`/`device`), and `torch.Event` has no `enable_timing`/`blocking`/`interprocess` (it has `record`/`query`/`synchronize`/`wait`). Nothing in `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer` reads `.cuda_stream` after this patch, and the sites that need CUDA-specific objects (NCCL `stream=` arguments, `torch.cuda.Stream(...)` constructors, `get_device_properties`, `ipc_collect`) correctly stay `torch.cuda.*`.

### pre-commit and DCO

`pre-commit run --files <the six files>` on the cluster head node: **exit 0** — 14 hooks passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed, including `Prevent new 'torch.cuda' APIs call`, `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, SPDX headers, forbidden imports, lazy imports and config-defaults. The hooks whose toolchains (cargo/node/go) are absent on this image were skipped via `SKIP=typos,markdownlint-cli2,actionlint,rust-cargo-fmt`.

Both commits carry `Signed-off-by:`; GitHub's `DCO` and `pre-commit` checks are green on `6f0df167`.

### Not verified

- **The 4-GPU sharded-RDT example** (`examples/rl/rlhf_sharded_rdt_small_ep.py`) did not complete, for environment reasons: the trainer fails at `register_nixl_memory` (`Failed to register cuda memory with NIXL ...`), and direct probes show NIXL's CUDA backend is unusable on this image — `import nixl` needs `libssl.so.3`, which the node image (glibc 2.32) does not provide in a compatible build, and with a compatible `libssl.so.3` the `nixl_agent` constructor segfaults. So `sharded_rdt_engine._ensure_proc_worker` / `_process_item` / `_run_quant` and the CUDA branch of `sharded_rdt_trainer._pack_group_for_export` are covered by the suite above plus the equivalence checks, **not** by a real weight sync over NIXL.
- ROCm/XPU and torch versions other than 2.13.0.
- No performance or output-quality claim: this replaces equivalent APIs and no kernel or model-level benchmark was run.

✅ @Ronald1995, CI is now available for this PR.

- `/ci run` starts upstream CI; `/amd-ci run` starts AMD CI only.
- Run commands test your branch with every commit currently on its upstream target branch. If it is behind, the bot merges the target branch into it first (pull before pushing again). Append `--allow-stale` to a run command to test an outdated branch as is, at your own risk.
- `/ci retry` retries failed jobs in the CI build for the current PR head. If the current head has no CI build, it starts a new CI build for the current head containing only jobs that failed in the latest earlier CI build for this PR.
- `/amd-ci retry` retries failed jobs in AMD CI for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` when the current head has no AMD CI build.
- `/ci cancel` cancels scheduled or running CI builds for this PR branch; `/amd-ci cancel` does the same for AMD CI only.

<!-- vllm-ci-authorized -->

### CI: `amd-mi355-dpx-benchmarks-cli` is a pre-existing failure, not caused by this PR

The only red job in build #97033 fails in
`tests/benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py::test_request_payload_is_accepted_by_the_server_schema`
with `KeyError: 'x-request-id'` (the rest of that job is 224 passed, 1 skipped). This PR
only touches `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer`; the same test fails identically when run
against the pristine **merge-base** wheel (`7a64fb8fc9`, none of this PR's files), so it is
red on main, not here.

**Root cause:** aiohttp 3.14.5 / multidict 7.1.0 / yarl 1.25.1 (bumped by #62835)
canonicalize outgoing header names, so the test's server receives `X-Request-ID` instead of
`x-request-id`. The test copies `request.headers` — a case-insensitive `CIMultiDictProxy` —
into a plain `dict` and then looks the key up case-sensitively. Reproduced directly:
with aiohttp 3.14.5 the handler captures `{"X-Request-ID": "bench-7", "Content-Type": ...}`.

**A fix is already open:** #63462 replaces `dict(request.headers)` with
`request.headers.copy()`. I re-ran the test file with that one-line change on the same
aiohttp 3.14.5: `1 failed` before, `24 passed` after — on both this PR's tree and the
merge-base tree. Nothing to change here; the job should go green once #63462 lands.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## H20 correctness verification — `6f0df167` (2× H20e, torch 2.13.0+cu130)

Verified the PR head `6f0df1675fa109e892c33ee72e7b6cc9ca97e656` (branch `codex/weight-transfer-accelerator`, unmodified; change commit `09dce8f7` on top of merged main `7a64fb8fc9`) on the SGP H20 cluster, node `vllm-sgp-h20-04`, 2-GPU jobs (NVIDIA H20-3e 143 GB, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130).

### Environment

- vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev441+g7a64fb8fc` — the per-commit wheel of the **merge base** (`7a64fb8fc9`) from `wheels.vllm.ai`, installed with `uv pip install --no-deps` into a copy of a prepared CUDA venv, plus `ray==2.56.1`, `nixl==1.5.0`, `orjson`.
- The six changed files were then copied over the installed package, and a pristine copy of the same wheel was kept as the baseline, so both trees are identical apart from this patch.

| file | PR md5 | baseline md5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ipc_engine.py` | `36bfff84` | `a3abe286` |
| `nccl_engine.py` | `8978915f` | `a7a67fa5` |
| `packed_tensor.py` | `a2636c6b` | `e6e18f7b` |
| `sharded_rdt_engine.py` | `aead682b` | `80a7ead0` |
| `sharded_rdt_trainer.py` | `1549c6fa` | `2daa5dad` |
| `sparse_nccl_engine.py` | `e7344617` | `2283b787` |

### Test suite: PR and baseline are identical

```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --import-mode=importlib --no-header -rA \
  tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_plan.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_trainer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_producer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer_m2n.py \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer_nccl_uid.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py
```

| tree | result |
| --- | --- |
| PR | 6 failed, 464 passed, 26 skipped (17:07) |
| merge base `7a64fb8fc9` | 6 failed, 464 passed, 26 skipped (17:01) |

The same six tests fail on both trees with the same messages, so none is caused by this change:

- `test_sharded_rdt_plan.py::TestBakeOnARealModel[gqa-dense|moe|mla-moe]` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'orjson'` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py:10`). The wheel was installed with `--no-deps` on this host; after adding `orjson` all three **pass** on both trees.
- `test_weight_transfer_m2n.py::test_m2n_weight_transfer_between_processes[tcp|uid]` → `nccl._extensions.bindings.nccl_m2n.NCCLReshardError: NCCL Reshard error code 5: NCCL operation queryResult failed: invalid usage`. The m2n engine is not touched by this PR and fails identically on the baseline.
- `test_weight_transfer_nccl_uid.py::test_nccl_weight_transfer_between_processes_uid` → failed with `ray.exceptions.GetTimeoutError` inside the full pass on both trees, and **passes** on both in the rerun below, i.e. environment/load sensitivity rather than this change.

Rerun of only those six tests after `orjson` was added: PR **4 passed, 2 failed**; baseline **4 passed, 2 failed**, the two failures being the m2n cases above.

The 26 skips are environmental: 23 × `modelexpress_rl` not installed, 2 × m2n variants that need 3/4 GPUs, 1 × `cupy` missing.

### Runtime API equivalence on H20 (7/7 pass)

`torch.accelerator.current_stream()` returns a generic `torch.Stream` on torch 2.13, so these are behaviour checks of each substituted call against its `torch.cuda.*` counterpart:

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `current_stream()` is the default stream (drains already-enqueued default-stream work) | pass |
| `current_stream(torch.device)` targets that device and does not change the current device | pass |
| `device_index(int)` context manager sets and restores the current device, including tensor placement | pass |
| `set_device_index(int)` inside a worker thread (engine proc/quant-thread pattern) | pass |
| `torch.Event()` `record`/`synchronize`/`wait` on `torch.cuda.Stream`s, with cross-stream ordering | pass |
| `torch.Event()` built on one thread, recorded on the proc stream, waited on the quant stream (engine pattern) | pass |
| `accelerator.synchronize()` drains default-stream work (4.7 ms vs 4.5 ms for `cuda.synchronize()` over the same matmul) | pass |

Compatibility observation that backs the PR's design note: on torch 2.13 the generic wrappers do **not** carry the CUDA-only attributes — `torch.Stream` has no `.cuda_stream` (it has `synchronize`/`query`/`record_event`/`wait_stream`/`device`), and `torch.Event` has no `enable_timing`/`blocking`/`interprocess` (it has `record`/`query`/`synchronize`/`wait`). Nothing in `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer` reads `.cuda_stream` after this patch, and the sites that need CUDA-specific objects (NCCL `stream=` arguments, `torch.cuda.Stream(...)` constructors, `get_device_properties`, `ipc_collect`) correctly stay `torch.cuda.*`.

### pre-commit and DCO

`pre-commit run --files <the six files>` on the cluster head node: **exit 0** — 14 hooks passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed, including `Prevent new 'torch.cuda' APIs call`, `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, SPDX headers, forbidden imports, lazy imports and config-defaults. The hooks whose toolchains (cargo/node/go) are absent on this image were skipped via `SKIP=typos,markdownlint-cli2,actionlint,rust-cargo-fmt`.

Both commits carry `Signed-off-by:`; GitHub's `DCO` and `pre-commit` checks are green on `6f0df167`.

### Not verified

- **The 4-GPU sharded-RDT example** (`examples/rl/rlhf_sharded_rdt_small_ep.py`) did not complete, for environment reasons: the trainer fails at `register_nixl_memory` (`Failed to register cuda memory with NIXL ...`), and direct probes show NIXL's CUDA backend is unusable on this image — `import nixl` needs `libssl.so.3`, which the node image (glibc 2.32) does not provide in a compatible build, and with a compatible `libssl.so.3` the `nixl_agent` constructor segfaults. So `sharded_rdt_engine._ensure_proc_worker` / `_process_item` / `_run_quant` and the CUDA branch of `sharded_rdt_trainer._pack_group_for_export` are covered by the suite above plus the equivalence checks, **not** by a real weight sync over NIXL.
- ROCm/XPU and torch versions other than 2.13.0.
- No performance or output-quality claim: this replaces equivalent APIs and no kernel or model-level benchmark was run.

### CI: `amd-mi355-dpx-benchmarks-cli` is a pre-existing failure, not caused by this PR

The only red job in build #97033 fails in
`tests/benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py::test_request_payload_is_accepted_by_the_server_schema`
with `KeyError: 'x-request-id'` (the rest of that job is 224 passed, 1 skipped). This PR
only touches `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer`; the same test fails identically when run
against the pristine **merge-base** wheel (`7a64fb8fc9`, none of this PR's files), so it is
red on main, not here.

**Root cause:** aiohttp 3.14.5 / multidict 7.1.0 / yarl 1.25.1 (bumped by #62835)
canonicalize outgoing header names, so the test's server receives `X-Request-ID` instead of
`x-request-id`. The test copies `request.headers` — a case-insensitive `CIMultiDictProxy` —
into a plain `dict` and then looks the key up case-sensitively. Reproduced directly:
with aiohttp 3.14.5 the handler captures `{"X-Request-ID": "bench-7", "Content-Type": ...}`.

**A fix is already open:** #63462 replaces `dict(request.headers)` with
`request.headers.copy()`. I re-ran the test file with that one-line change on the same
aiohttp 3.14.5: `1 failed` before, `24 passed` after — on both this PR's tree and the
merge-base tree. Nothing to change here; the job should go green once #63462 lands.
